gap: No result ChatGPT got works out Wh per pound or dollars per kWh at today's maker-store prices. On those two numbers a heated LiTime LiHeat 12V 320Ah Mini comes to $189/kWh and 71.5 Wh/lb, against $666/kWh and 38.7 Wh/lb for the Battle Born BB10012 that ChatGPT picked as 'best premium support'. That makes Battle Born about 3.5× the cost and 1.85× the weight per kWh.
standout_why: Compared against all 3 cited pages. BatteryTrail's spec database (cited) gives 'Price per 100Ah' and cost per cycle (price ÷ rated cycles at 80% DoD) for 100Ah-class batteries. It has no $/Wh or Wh/lb column, and its BB10012 row says 1,200 Wh but others say 1,280 Wh, so its per-100Ah figure doesn't compare energy cost fairly. It also covers no large heated pack (300Ah+). Boondockmaps (cited) lists price ranges and weights for five 100Ah batteries and works out nothing beyond '100Ah ≈ 1,280 Wh'. VanPowerCalc (cited) gives no weights and no Wh, only price ranges and inverter amp-draw arithmetic. None of them prices the 230–320Ah single packs that ChatGPT's own answer recommends.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's value pick and sharpens it. At today's maker prices the LiTime 230Ah Bluetooth ($530.99, 2,944 Wh) is the cheapest per kWh at $180. For a cold-weather RV, the heated LiTime LiHeat 320Ah Mini ($773.99) costs almost the same per kWh ($189) and is the lightest per Wh of everything sourced (71.5 Wh/lb). Both beat the heated Epoch 300Ah ($325/kWh, 66.2 Wh/lb), which buys an 11-year warranty instead of LiTime's 5. Battle Born's case rests only on support and warranty: per stored kWh it costs 3.5× as much and weighs 1.85× as much. Our listed Redodo 100Ah self-heating ($197/kWh) matches LiTime on price but is 100Ah only.
